profile.org_note: Five reporting segments per the FY2025 10-K and July 2026 10-Q (North; Mid-Atlantic; South = Arkansas, Florida, South Carolina, Texas; Mountain; Pacific); management runs President/COO Seth Ring -> Regional Presidents (named: Todd Callahan Pacific, Mark Bailey Utah/Mountain, Tom Murray Florida, Rob Paul Texas & Arkansas; North and Mid-Atlantic not public) -> Group Presidents -> Division Presidents, and the South segment is split across at least two regional presidents. No corporate land head is published: land is sourced by division and regional land VPs (e.g. VP Land Acquisition Dustin Bowersett) and approved up the line to the COO/CEO, while land financing (options, land banking, JVs) sits with CFO Gregg Ziegler and Treasurer Ryan McKenna.
profile.summary: Largest US luxury builder: 11,292 homes delivered for $10.8 billion of home sales revenue in FY2025 (year ends October 31) at a $960,000 average price; FY2026 guidance is 10,500 to 10,600 deliveries at about $1.0 million. At July 31, 2026 it controlled 75,486 lots (31,817 owned, 43,669 optioned, 58% optioned) across 471 selling communities; the FY2025 10-K counts 24 states plus D.C., and Arkansas (Buffington Homes) was added in 2026. Management says it turns first to seller financing, joint ventures and traditional options and uses land banking 'carefully and modestly': about 20% of FY2026 revenue comes from land-banked communities and about 30% of optioned lots are land-banked. The whole top team changed in twelve months (CFO Nov 2025, CAO Feb 2026, CEO Mar 2026, President/COO Jun 2026, plus a new Treasurer), so relationships are being reset.

people.name: Karl K. Mistry
people.title: Chief Executive Officer
people.reports_to: Board of Directors (Douglas C. Yearley, Jr., Executive Chairman)
people.prior_role: Executive Vice President (2021-2026) over homebuilding in 15 eastern states; Regional President, Mid-Atlantic (2019); Group President, Metro Washington D.C. (2016); Division President, Houston (2012)
people.source_title: Toll Brothers IR: Senior Management page
people.note: CEO and director effective 2026-03-30 (8-K filed 2026-03-31, Item 5.02; appointment approved 2026-01-05). Joined 2004 through the executive training program as an Assistant Project Manager. Came up through division and regional operations in Texas and the Mid-Atlantic. On the May 2026 earnings call he said about 20% of FY2026 revenue comes from land-banked communities and about 30% of optioned lots are land-banked, and that 20% to 30% 'feels about right' going forward; his prepared remarks put seller financing, joint ventures and traditional options ahead of land banking, which Toll uses 'when it makes sense'.

people.name: Gregg Ziegler
people.title: Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer
people.prior_role: Senior Vice President, Investor Relations & Treasurer (Treasurer since 2013; added Investor Relations May 2024, with capital markets, M&A, corporate strategy, land financing and FP&A)
people.source_title: Toll Brothers IR: Senior Management page
people.note: CFO effective 2025-11-01, succeeding Martin P. Connor (8-K filed 2025-07-11). Leads accounting, treasury and finance, tax, investor relations, risk management, internal audit, mortgage and title. As Treasurer he ran capital markets and land financing, so he is the senior decision-maker on land-banking and lot-option structures. The July 2025 8-K says the CFO reports directly to the Chairman and CEO (then Yearley); the CEO role passed to Mistry in March 2026, so the current line is inferred. Still listed as the investor contact with this email and phone on the 2026-11-10 earnings-webcast release (the 2026-08-18 earnings release gave (215) 478-3820). Signed the February 2026 revolving-credit amendment (Mizuho as agent) as EVP and CFO.
